title: Scanning the Swollen Macula

patient.name: Mr Hassan bin Yusof
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for a macular OCT scan because of blurred central vision; has diabetes

history.hpc: Mr Hassan is referred for a macular OCT to assess blurred central vision in both eyes, worse on the right. He says: 'Doctor say my sugar high, my middle vision blur, ask me come do this scan.' He has diabetes with sub-optimal control. No pain or redness. The OT's task is to acquire a good-quality macular OCT and document the findings for the doctor.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes (HbA1c high), hypertension. Known diabetic retinopathy under monitoring.
history.social_hx: Taxi driver; long driving hours. Non-smoker.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Clear media adequate for imaging; mild lens changes
examination_findings.fundus: Diabetic retinopathy with suspected macular oedema, right worse than left — for OCT and doctor review

investigations.macular_oct: Macular cube/line OCT acquired both eyes. Right eye shows increased central retinal/macular thickness with intraretinal fluid (cystoid spaces) consistent with diabetic macular oedema. Scan acquired with good signal strength and correct centration on the fovea. Findings documented with the scan pattern used.
investigations.scan_quality: Signal strength adequate; fixation stable; foveal centration confirmed before saving.

diagnosis: Macular OCT shows diabetic macular oedema (worse in the right eye) — increased macular thickness with intraretinal fluid. The OT competency is correct acquisition (centration, focus, signal strength) and accurate documentation; diagnosis and treatment are the doctor's.

immediate: Confirm the diagnosis/indication (diabetic, blurred central vision) and which eye(s) to scan
Explain the OCT is a quick, non-contact light scan and position the patient with chin/forehead on the rest
Ensure correct focus and centration on the fovea, and check signal strength before saving
Acquire the macular scan for both eyes and re-acquire if fixation loss or low signal degrades quality
Document diagnosis, indication, eye(s), scan pattern, and findings (central thickness, fluid) for the doctor
Avoid interpreting/treating — present the quality-checked scan for doctor review
follow_up: Doctor to confirm diabetic macular oedema and decide on treatment (e.g., anti-VEGF/laser)
Baseline scan saved for comparison at future visits
Encourage diabetic control and regular review
patient_education: Explain the scan is painless and only takes a short time, no eye drops needed for this scan
Ask him to keep his chin steady and look at the fixation target
Explain the doctor will review the scan and discuss results and any treatment
Encourage good blood sugar control to protect his vision

key_points: Confirms the indication (diabetes, blurred central vision) and eye(s) to scan
Checks diabetic control/retinopathy context relevant to the scan
Confirms no contraindication to imaging and adequate media
Explains the procedure to gain cooperation
Positions the patient correctly and ensures correct focus and foveal centration
Checks signal strength/quality before saving and re-acquires if poor
Acquires the appropriate macular scan pattern for both eyes
Documents diagnosis, indication, eye(s), scan pattern, and findings
Recognises increased macular thickness with intraretinal fluid as macular oedema
Identifies the right eye as more affected
Understands the OT role is acquisition and documentation, not diagnosis
Defers treatment decisions to the doctor
Produces a quality-checked, well-centred scan for both eyes
Documents the scan details and findings accurately
Explains the scan to the patient and gains cooperation
Hands the scan to the doctor and saves a baseline for comparison
